title: Principal Officer, Designated Director, Staff Training and Independent Audit

paragraphs.text: Reference is invited to the governance requirements under the anti-money laundering framework. This circular clarifies the duties of the Principal Officer and the Designated Director, and prescribes requirements for staff training and independent audit of KYC and AML compliance in banks.

Designated Director: every bank shall nominate a whole-time director, or the Managing Director, as the Designated Director responsible for overall compliance with KYC and AML obligations, and shall communicate the name and contact details of the Designated Director to the Financial Intelligence Unit within 30 days of appointment.

Principal Officer duties: the Principal Officer shall be an officer not below the rank of General Manager, responsible for monitoring transactions, furnishing Cash Transaction Reports and Suspicious Transaction Reports, and acting as the point of contact for the Financial Intelligence Unit; the Principal Officer shall not head any business vertical.

Change of Principal Officer: any change in the Principal Officer shall be communicated to the Financial Intelligence Unit within 15 days of the change, and the position of Principal Officer shall not remain vacant for more than 30 days.

Staff training on KYC and AML: every bank shall conduct KYC and AML training for all front-line, operations and compliance staff at least once a year, and every newly recruited staff member shall complete induction training on KYC and AML within 60 days of joining.

Independent audit of KYC: the KYC and AML policies and procedures of every bank shall be subjected to an independent audit by an audit function independent of the business units at least once a year, and the audit findings shall be placed before the Audit Committee of the Board within one quarter.

Board oversight of KYC and AML: the Designated Director shall place a report on KYC and AML compliance, including the status of re-KYC, Cash Transaction Report and Suspicious Transaction Report filings and audit findings, before the Board at least once every six months. These provisions are effective from July 1, 2022.
